title: Quantity class constrained value interpretation
summary: A form class constrains whether a value is cardinal, indexed-share, open-level or quality-grade. This is a raw unreviewed semantic hypothesis, not a confirmed reading.

design.unit: exact whole-form or complete construction occurrences in the cited source scope
design.contrast: The same value family is interpreted only within its predeclared class: cardinal forms cannot be silently exchanged with open value or quality-grade forms
design.prediction: The same value family is interpreted only within its predeclared class: cardinal forms cannot be silently exchanged with open value or quality-grade forms
design.countermodel: Renderer defaults and inherited score labels may create the apparent classes without a semantic quantity distinction
design.falsifier: A held cross-class comparison shows cardinal/open/grade forms interchangeable under the same local frames; stop the class-constraint hypothesis
design.principal_risk: The cited report supplies structural or working observations, not independently bound Voynich meaning; required semantic endpoints may be unavailable.
design.related: Near GDT729 and IDEA000049; focuses mutually restricted value classes rather than unit calibration.

source_evidence.quote:
GDT729 resolves the fourteen forms explicitly named by the current route. The
result is five cardinal amounts, one amount inside an indexed share, seven
open value levels and one quality grade. None remains a slash-separated
non-answer, and none is put on HOLD.
